claims: Surface recombination of plasma radicals is generally considered to limit film conformality during plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition (ALD).
Film penetration into high-aspect-ratio structures can give direct information on the recombination probability r of plasma radicals on the growth surface.
A strong material dependence has been observed for recombination of oxygen (O) atoms on SiO2, TiO2, Al2O3, and HfO2.
Films of SiO2 and TiO2 penetrated extremely deep up to an aspect ratio (AR) of ∼ 900 using extended plasma exposures.
Similar surface recombination probabilities of r = (6 ± 2) × 10 -5 and (7 ± 4) × 10 -5 were determined for SiO2 and TiO2 processes.
Growth of Al2O3 and HfO2 was conformal up to depths corresponding to ARs of ∼ 80 and ∼ 40, respectively.

Quantitative insight into surface recombination is essential for modeling radical-surface interaction and understanding for which materials and conditions conformal film growth is feasible by plasma-assisted ALD.
The film penetration depth into high-AR structures is generally limited by surface recombination.
An exponential increase in plasma exposure time is required to linearly increase the film penetration when limited by surface recombination.
Low values of r on the order of 10 -5 were determined for SiO2 and TiO2, corresponding to extremely deep film penetration approaching an AR of ∼ 900 at long plasma exposures.
Plasma ALD of Al2O3 and HfO2 was limited to ARs of ∼ 80 and ∼ 40, respectively, with r lying in the range of 10 -3 up to 10 -1.
There is a strong material dependence in the surface recombination of plasma radicals and film conformality during plasma ALD.
For the investigated processes, especially for SiO2 and TiO2, r seems sufficiently low to meet very demanding conformality requirements.
